## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trial results yet, and the starting network scored 0.000 on both seeds. Read closely, the starting design looks capable of the task. Its 1×1 stem can learn "target cell missing at the column's current height". Its max/min/average pooling over each brick footprint can learn the landing height and whether all cells under the brick are missing. So the zero score more likely comes from the training budget. The default recipe gives about 131k steps in batches of 4,096, which is only 32 PPO policy updates. That is very few for exact multi-brick builds. The +1 exact-build bonus also comes at the end of the episode, and gamma 0.95 discounts it heavily. This round tests: (A) the starting network with 2 epochs, more updates and a longer horizon; (C) the same with 1 epoch, to measure the epochs trade-off; (B) a stronger 2D network under recipe A, with GroupNorm residual blocks, a skip from per-cell stem features to the placement head, and separate DONE and value heads.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, on both seeds. That held for 1, 2 and 4 PPO epochs, with and without GroupNorm residual blocks, and with gamma 0.99. More updates alone did not help. My main guess is that the policy collapses to DONE early. A near-random policy gets negative reward from extra cells on most placements, and DONE gives 0. So DONE gets reinforced before the network learns which placements land on missing target cells, and ent_coef 0.005 does little to stop this. A second guess is that the PoolHead's max/min/avg pooling throws away the exact per-cell layout of a footprint, which matters for landing height. This round tests a higher entropy bonus on the starting network as a single change, and two runs of a new architecture with a learned footprint-kernel head: one with 1 epoch, one with 2 epochs and a lower learning rate.

### Round 3
Six trials, and every one scored 0 on both dev and training success. That covers the starting net and a residual GroupNorm net, both pool heads and footprint-kernel heads, 1 to 2 epochs, entropy 0.005 to 0.02, and 157k to 408k steps. Training success staying at 0 even with 400k steps means the problem is not greedy sharpness or seed luck. Something basic is mismatched. All six networks share one untested assumption: each brick type's logit at grid cell (y,x) maps to action index t*Y*X+y*X+x, with the anchor at the brick's top-left. The task warns that the world may differ from its description. If the real action layout or anchor differs (for example transposed or offset), a translation-equivariant spatial head cannot learn the mapping. Round 3 therefore tests layout-agnostic heads: a learned linear map from all cells to all actions, with the legality mask fed in as learned input so the net can tell from legal anchors which action is which. Recipe stays fixed: 2 epochs, gamma 0.99.

### Round 4
Nine trials covered recipe changes (1, 2 or 4 epochs, ent 0.005-0.02, lr 5e-4 to 1e-3), normalisation and residual blocks, footprint-kernel heads, flat layout-agnostic heads and a plain MLP. All scored 0 dev success and 0 training success on both seeds. Since even the layout-agnostic MLP never builds anything exactly, the problem is probably not the head or the action layout. My best guess is that the policy learns to call DONE immediately. Random early placements mostly fill cells outside the target, so carrying on looks costly (about -0.04 per step, roughly -1.3 over an episode), while DONE returns 0. DONE is one logit shared by every state, so it can win before placements learn to fill target cells. A bigger entropy bonus (0.02) did not prevent this. Untested fix: make the DONE logit learn more slowly with a fixed output temperature (scale 0.1). This is an architectural constant, not hand-set weights. I combine it with a low-gamma recipe and with the residual net.
